_meta.purpose: Supplement the hand-written boundary cases in tests/api/test_invoices_api.py with additional edge cases an AI assistant suggested, to broaden coverage beyond what one person thinks of unassisted.
_meta.status_2026_09: All originally-ambiguous cases except ai-003 have now been resolved through manual testing against the real Xero Demo Company (both UI and API) and converted from pytest.skip() into real assertions -- see individual review_note fields for what was found. ai-003 (amount sent as a JSON string) remains open at the API layer specifically; the UI-level input masking observed doesn't answer what the API does with a string-typed UnitAmount.

invoice_amount_cases.description: Extremely large amount — tests for integer overflow or formatting bugs at scale
invoice_amount_cases.review_note: Kept as-is. Xero's documented numeric field limits accommodate this; worth confirming the UI renders it without truncation.

invoice_amount_cases.description: Amount with more than 2 decimal places — tests rounding/truncation behaviour
invoice_amount_cases.review_note: Manually verified via Xero's web UI (2026-09): entering 10.999 is accepted, not rejected -- Xero rounds rather than enforcing a hard 2-decimal-place limit. Promoted from 'ambiguous' to an active assertion, but note this is UI-observed behaviour; the API test below sends this value directly to the API's JSON payload, which is a genuinely separate validation path from the UI's number input. If the API test disagrees with this UI finding (e.g. rejects it, or rounds it differently), that itself is a real UI-vs-API validation discrepancy worth its own xfail finding, not a bug in this test.

invoice_amount_cases.description: Amount as a string instead of a number in the JSON payload — tests type coercion
invoice_amount_cases.review_note: Still genuinely ambiguous, and NOT resolved by the manual UI testing done so far. What was manually observed: the Xero web UI's amount field simply refuses to accept a quote character or any non-numeric keystroke at all -- that's client-side input masking on the text box, which happens before anything is ever sent as a request, and produced no server response to learn from. It says nothing about how Xero's API behaves when a JSON payload deliberately sends UnitAmount as the string "100.00" instead of the number 100.00, since that path never goes through a keyboard filter -- it's pure JSON parsing on Xero's server. Kept ambiguous specifically for the API layer; this project's own API test below (test_ai_generated_cases.py) actually exercises this exact scenario against the real API, so running pytest is what will resolve it, not more UI testing.

invoice_amount_cases.description: Amount just above the zero boundary at higher precision (0.001)
invoice_amount_cases.review_note: Manually verified via Xero's web UI (2026-09): 0.001 is accepted, consistent with ai-002's finding that Xero doesn't hard-enforce 2 decimal places. Promoted from 'ambiguous'. Same caveat as ai-002 applies: this confirms UI behaviour, and the API test below is what actually confirms or contradicts it for the API layer specifically.

contact_name_cases.description: Name with only whitespace — tests whether trimming happens before the completeness check
contact_name_cases.review_note: Kept and considered an important addition — the hand-written test only covered a fully empty string, not a whitespace-only string that LOOKS non-empty to a naive length check.

contact_name_cases.description: Name with only emoji characters — tests Unicode handling and completeness rule interaction
contact_name_cases.name: 😀👍
contact_name_cases.review_note: CONFIRMED via manual testing (2026-09): Xero accepts an emoji-only contact name without any validation error. Promoted from 'ambiguous' to an active assertion.
